body:
Triage set: P8, enhancement, area:post, effort:max, needs-research.

Reasons. The writer works on an output format that is not in the tree (Klartext .H), and it must be built from published manuals. That is the effort:max row. Posted G-code is under the safety floor anyway. The three questions are open, so the issue is research, not code: Pick will not take it for code. No source:agent label: the issue came from your GitHub account.

Related work: #3095 tests the DIN/ISO post; #2227 proposes the Klartext reader.

## Research findings for maintainer review

### 1. Select output by documented release and installed capability

For the first contribution, we propose an exact match for iTNC 530 NC software `340490-03`. Keep one Klartext writer. Add another release to the supported set when its manual documents the forms that the writer uses. Record the manual sections, required options, and test results for that release. An unknown release or missing capability should produce a diagnostic before writing the file.

Two examples show why this matters.

- Both manuals describe preset Cycle 247 with `Q339`. Only populated preset axes take a new value, and Test Run does not activate the preset. See SW03 p. 492 and SW04 p. 519.
- SW04 adds `Q403` to Cycle 209 for the spindle speed during withdrawal. It also introduces `PATTERN DEF`. A later tapping implementation would need a rule for that parameter. Tapping stays outside the proposed first contribution.

The SW03 manual also lists functions controlled by the installed Feature Content Level (p. 8). An NC software update alone does not enable every function. [SW03 manual, 533 190-22](https://content.heidenhain.de/doku/tnc_guide/pdf_files/iTNC530/34049x-neu/en/bhb.pdf) · [SW04 manual, 533 190-23, release changes and Cycle 209](https://content.heidenhain.de/doku/tnc_guide/pdf_files/iTNC530/34049x-04/en/533_190-23.pdf)

### 2. Separate the installation facts from the language rules

The machine file should identify the installed control, NC release, axes and manual tool-change procedure. Reuse existing machine fields for spindle and coolant data. Add an option or Feature Content Level field when a supported operation needs it. CamCraft should own the mapping from those facts to the blocks and parameters it emits.

For example, `M140 MB MAX` retracts along the active tool axis toward the active traverse limit. Collision monitoring can shorten that move. Reaching the Picomax's physical tool-change position and switching the drives off are installation requirements. The release number cannot establish either condition. Stock bounds and the selected preset are job data. Use the modeled stock bottom for `BLK FORM`. [SW03 manual, §7.4, p. 303](https://content.heidenhain.de/doku/tnc_guide/pdf_files/iTNC530/34049x-neu/en/bhb.pdf)

### 3. Proposed contribution after agreement

We propose one implementation issue and one draft PR for the first usable combination. It would deliver the machine definition, standalone CamCraft post, required stock data, and tests together. Support one metric setup, XYZ linear moves, and constant-height XY arcs. Include positive and refusal tests through the app and CLI. Check that existing DIN/ISO output stays byte-identical. If the maintainers prefer separate review for the machine schema, we can split that prerequisite from the writer.

The local prototype refused both `340490-04` and `606425-04` when configured as targets. The programming station running `606425-04 SP20` accepted and ran the two programs emitted for `340490-03`. It reached all three and five programmed stops, respectively, and both programs reached the end. These tests cover those samples on the station release. They leave the physical preset, drive state, coolant operation and tool-change clearance open on the Picomax.

**Decision requested:** Do the maintainers agree with the exact first target, the division of machine and post data, and the proposed PR scope? What physical-machine evidence do they require before merging or marking the installation as machine-tested?

The maintainer answered the three questions of this proposal on 2026-11-21.

1. NC software match: the first release requires an exact match of the control and the NC software release. A different release refuses the job before it writes a file. A release joins the list when someone shows evidence that its syntax is the same (a manual page or a station run).
2. Where the facts live: the machine file holds the facts of the machine itself. These are the control, the NC software release, the installed options and the tool-change procedure (manual or changer). The post and its tests hold the syntax of the control and the cycle-parameter rules.
3. Go: yes. Submit the work in two pull requests. First the machine-definition changes as a small PR. Then the post with its golden output and refusal tests as a second PR. Include the manual references, the station results and the outstanding machine checks in the PRs.

The scope of the first post stays as proposed: one metric setup, three linear axes, stock bounds, preset, straight moves, plunges and constant-height XY arcs. Everything else is refused by name.

The issue stays at P8 until the first PR is open. Each PR gets the P label of the issue it fixes and a `Refs #3098` line.
The machine definition is tracked in #3181. The Klartext post and its tests are tracked in #3182. I will submit the machine definition first. The two issues list the requested labels for triage.

The maintainers approved the release match, the machine data and the scope in this issue. Both implementation issues are complete. PR #3204 merged the machine definition for #3181 in ad0307b7a. PR #3231 merged the Klartext writer for #3182 in 910474bc9. The first supported target is the Fehlmann Picomax 55 with iTNC 530 NC software 340490-03. The two sample programs passed on the programming station. The physical Picomax checks remain open as listed in #3231.
